text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

French financier JACQUES NECKER, who was imprisoned in The Bastille for suggesting that the aristocracy pay taxes, was born in 1732. The people of Paris agreed with him, and later stormed the building and freed him.

English sportsman JOHN MYTTON, who kept two-thousand dogs, 50 cats and a pet bear, was born in 1796. He was quite an individual, and had a habit of drinking a bottle of port every morning, while shaving. He also had an unusual cure for hiccups - He would set his nightshirt on fire with a candle to give himself the required fright, to scare off the hiccups !
South Australian editor of the 'Adelaide Observer' JOHN STEPHENS, who once claimed that "certain moral felonies were punishable only through the press", was born in 1806.
German author of "Sodom's End", HERMANN SUDERMANN, was born in 1857.

Australian cricketer ERNEST "Jonah" JONES was born in 1869. He was our first fast-bowler, and put a ball through W.C.GRACE's beard in his 1896 debut international game. He also once broke the ribs of a batsman.
Russian-born American film director LEWIS MILESTONE, who won an Oscar for "All Quiet On The Western Front", was born in 1895.

American novelist and short story writer TRUMAN CAPOTE, whose books included "Breakfast At Tifanny's", was born in 1924. The Australian commander in Vietnam, Major-General ALAN STRETTON, was born in 1922. He also ran the relief operation for Darwin, in the aftermath of Cyclone Tracy.
American actress ANGIE DICKINSON, who became famous while starring in the tv series "Police Woman", was born in 1931.
American singer JOHNNY MATHIS was born in 1935. He had many hits including "Chances Are" (1957) and "When A Child Is Born" (1976).
American singer/songwriter FRANKIE LYMON, who had a hit with "Why Do Fools Fall In Love" (1956) at the age of just 14, was born in 1942. He died on the 28th of February, 1968 of a drug overdose.
American drummer DEWEY MARTIN, who played with the group 'Buffalo Springfield', was born in 1942.

American singer MARILYN McCOO, who sang with the 'Fifth Dimension', was born in 1943. She had hits with "Up, Up And Away" (1967), "Aquarius/Let The Sunshine In" (1969) and "I Didn't Get To Sleep" (1972). She married BILLY DAVIS JNR from the group in 1969, and recorded the million- seller duet "You Don't Have To Be A Star (To Be In My Show) in 1976. MARILYN later became the hostess of the tv show 'Solid Gold'.

British singer MARC BOLAN (MARC FELD) was born in 1947. He formed 'T-Rex' in 1967, whose hits included "Debora" (1968), "Hot Love" (1971), "Get It On" (1971), "Metal Guru" (1972) and "Children Of The Revolution" (1972). BOLAN died in a car crash on the 16th of September, 1977.
** EVENTS **
1630 : JOHN BILLINGTON was executed in New Plymouth for murder, the first capital crime in America.
1882 : Water power was used for the first time to generate electricity, at a plant on the Fox River near Appleton, in the American state of Wisconsin.
1888 : ACK the Ripper killed two more prostitutes in the
streets of London's East End, his 3rd and 4th victims. Police had made little headway in the case, and feared the Ripper would strike again.

1927 : BABE RUTH (GEORGE HERMAN RUTH) hit his 60th home run of the season, setting an all-time American baseball record. The New York Yankees' star smashed the record at TOM ZACHARY pitch in a game against the Washington Senators. The "Sultan of Swat" broke his own previous record of 59 home runs set in 1921 - which in turn broke the record 54 he hit in 1920. Before joining the Yankees, RUTH broke records as a pitcher for the Boston Red Sox.
1933 : American President FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT announced 700-million dollars in an aid package for the country's poor called "New Deal".

1938 : British Prime Minister NEVILLE CHAMBERLAIN returned from the Munich Conference declaring that the agreement had achieved "peace with honour". The Germans had sought occupation of parts of Czechoslovakia following a series of riots. The Czechs called the agreement "treachery".
1949 : MAO TSE-TUNG formally became chairman of the Peoples' Republic of China.

1955 : Hollywood screen idol JAMES DEAN died in a car crash. The 24 year old died like he lived - fast. He crashed his Porsche Spider while on his way to compete in a motor race outside Los Angeles. Compared to MARLON BRANDO on screen, he starred in just three films, "East Of Eden " (1955), "Rebel Without A Cause" (1955) and "Giant" (1956), in which he starred opposite ROCK HUDSON. Ironically, just a few weeks before his death, DEAN had made a public service film, advising youngsters to drive safely.
1957 : The remains of Captain BLIGH's "Bounty" were found off Pitcairn Island in the Pacific Ocean.
1960 : Fifteen new African nations were admitted to the United nations.
1962 : Angry whites stormed the University of Mississippi campus, protesting at the enrollment of the first black student, JAMES MEREDITH.
1970 : Britain swapped hijack hostages for Palestinian terrorist LEILA KHALED.

1971 : An inquiry was announced into a prison riot in New York state which left 32 inmates and ten warders dead. More than one thousand prisoners had taken guards hostage at the Attica State Correction Facility, before the jail was stormed by state troops.
1975 : Boxer MUHAMMAD ALI defeated JOE FRAZIER in the Philippines, to retain his world heavyweight crown.
1980 : CLIFF DOLAN succeeded BOB HAWKE as Australian ACTU President, after HAWKE announced his intention to run for parliament at the coming October federal election.
1981 : Victorian police sealed the centre of Melbourne, for the start of the Commonwealth Heads Of Government Meeting (CHOGM).
1982 : PRINCE PHILLIP opened the Commonwealth Games in Brisbane.
1988 : Canadian sprinter BEN JOHNSON was stripped of his 100-metres gold medal at the Seoul Olympic Games after failing a drug test. JOHNSON was flown home to Canada in disgrace.
1988 : An inquest jury found that the IRA gang, shot dead in March, was unlawfully killed by British S.A.S soliders.
1989 : American composer, music critic and conductor VIRGIL THOMSON died.
1990 : The British Army shot dead two joy-riding teenagers in Belfast.

1994 : A 101-year-old Gold Coast swimmer MARY MAINA broke the 50-metres freestyle record for women aged 90-and-over at the World Masters Games in Brisbane. She swam the distance in five-minutes, 10.84 seconds.
